title: SAML: consent-driven JIT user lifecycle with MFA handoff and deterministic logout
creator: Lina Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a deterministic orchestration for SAML-initiated sessions that: (1) performs Just-In-Time (JIT) provisioning with a user consent step when required by policy, (2) ensures clear MFA expectations and handoff semantics for federated identities, and (3) provides deterministic logout/reauth behavior across browser sessions, API tokens, and dedicated/private deployments.

Scope and Acceptance Criteria:
- JIT provisioning flow that can surface a consent screen (or skip with policy) and records the consent event in audit logs.
- MFA handoff rules: when IdP asserts MFA, Redwood accepts; when IdP does not assert, platform enforces stepup per org policy (none/optional/required) with clear user-visible messaging.
- Logout propagation: SAML SLO and local session invalidation must coordinate so that logout of browser session invalidates short-lived API tokens and clears KV cache references for that principal.
- Re-auth policy: configurable re-auth interval and stepup triggers (sensitive routes, token renewal, admin actions).
- Backwards-compatible with existing SAML setups; incremental rollout with canary by org.
- Audit trail: every lifecycle event (JIT-consent, provisioned-role, MFA-decision, logout-signal, reauth) emits structured audit entries that map to our audit schema and include IdP assertion metadata.

Design Notes / Trade-offs:
- Consent UI will be hosted via Redwood Console for hosted customers; for Private deployments we provide a callback webhook that the tenant can surface in their own login flow. This avoids shipping per-tenant UI components but requires stronger webhook security and retries.
- We prefer to rely on the IdP's MFA assertion when present to reduce friction; however, for high-security orgs we will support an enforcement override that forces Redwood stepup even if IdP asserted MFA.
- Logout propagation may be eventually consistent for some edge cases (long-lived DB sessions or offline tokens). For those, we include a TTL-driven invalidation and an admin revocation API.

Rollout Plan:
1) Feature-flagged backend implementation + unit tests (internal integration only)
2) Canary with 2 low-risk customers and internal SSO test orgs, enable structured audit logging
3) Console consent UI rollout + documentation
4) Open rollout and add admin tooling for org-level reauth and revocation controls

Telemetry / Observability:
- New tracing spans: saml:jit:consent, saml:mfa:decision, saml:logout:propagate, saml:reauth:trigger
- Dashboards: per-org counts for JIT provisions, consent declines, MFA stepups, logout propagation failures
- Alerts: spike in consent declines or logout propagation error rate > 1%

Security Considerations:
- All consent and MFA decision events are immutable in the audit log and include hashed identifiers if requested by customer.
- Webhook callback for Private deployments must support signed payloads and replay protection.
- Ensure tokens thrown away on logout cannot be reused due to KV cache references; add best-effort cache purge and token blacklist fallback.
